_comment: How many extraction passes extract.py spends per posting, keyed on the platform the posting came from. One pass is the default and always was; a platform listed as below the agreement threshold gets three passes and a field-wise majority vote (extract.py's vote_facts()). This file holds no domain terms and no prompt text -- it is purely the per-source quality budget, so retargeting the pipeline does not touch it, and re-measuring self-consistency does.
_why: Task 06 measured deepseek-v4-flash disagreeing with ITSELF at temperature 0, and the disagreement is not spread evenly across sources -- it is concentrated in one. ai_involvement, which is the Pursuit cohort's entire targeting mechanism, self-agrees 92.2% on greenhouse/ashby and 77.8% on hn_whoishiring: a 14.4-point clean-versus-messy gap. Both branches of task 06's gate fired on that. Paying three calls where the model is unstable and one where it is not satisfies both with one mechanism, and it is a per-source budget rather than a global one precisely because the problem is per-source.
_measurement_provenance: Every number in measured_agreement comes from task 06, 2026-07-28: n=120 postings (115 comparable), --repeat 3, deepseek-v4-flash at temperature 0, on the frozen corpus-v2.jsonl fixture, all seven platforms represented. The metric is PAIRWISE agreement on ai_involvement -- the fraction of the three run-pairs per posting that gave the same answer -- not unanimous-of-3, which is stricter by construction and would not be comparable to the figures in docs/ingestion_tests/README.md. See DECISIONS.md '06 -- THE GATE'. These are agreement figures, NOT accuracy figures: a source could agree with itself perfectly and be wrong every time. They bound accuracy from above and nothing more.
_field_choice_note: Keyed on ai_involvement alone, though task 06 measured seniority_level (85.2%) and role_archetype (84.3%) too, both of which are lower in aggregate. ai_involvement is the field the cohort is targeted on, it is the one whose per-platform spread was measured, and a vote fixes every field at once anyway -- three passes cost the same whichever field justified them. Re-key this if the per-platform breakdown is ever measured for the other two.
_threshold_note: 0.90 is task 06's own gate line -- its table reads 'stop' for a field below 90% on the messy platform, and that is the branch that fired. Not a new number invented here. At 0.90 exactly one platform qualifies, and the six others sit at 91.1% or above, so the threshold is not near a cliff: moving it to 0.91 changes nothing, 0.92 would additionally pull in builtin (91.1%), and 0.93 would pull in greenhouse and ashby (92.2%) -- which is 9,659 of 11,824 rows and no longer a targeted remedy. Rejected: setting it at 0.95 'to be safe', which is the uniform majority-of-3 below under a different name.
_passes_note: Three, not two: two passes can only detect disagreement, never resolve it. Not five, which would be a 5x bill on the messiest source for the second-order gain of breaking three-way ties that a 3-way vote resolves by falling back to the first pass -- and the first pass is exactly what today's code already writes, so the fallback is never worse than the status quo.
_default_passes_note: A platform absent from measured_agreement gets ONE pass, deliberately. An unmeasured source is not a bad source; tripling its cost would be paying for a number nobody has. New sources therefore cost exactly what they cost today, and the way to give one three passes is to measure it (backend/evals, --repeat 3) and add the figure below -- not to guess. This is also what makes the file safe when a source is renamed: an unrecognised platform string degrades to today's behaviour rather than to a 3x bill.
_measured_agreement_caveats: lever's 1.000 is n=9 and means nothing on its own -- it is above the threshold and would be at one pass regardless, which is the only reason it is safe to record it here at face value. The platform value is 'builtin', not 'builtin-nyc' as several task files write it; the string here must match jobs.platform exactly or the lookup silently falls through to default_passes. That silent fall-through is why extract.py's test asserts the per-platform pass count rather than trusting this file to be read correctly.
_cost_arithmetic: Only hn_whoishiring qualifies at this threshold: 247 of 11,824 rows in the live table, 2.1%, counted 2026-07-28. Three passes on 2.1% of rows is 494 extra calls over a full re-extraction of the whole table -- +4.2% on the call count, not +200%. (2.1% is hn's SHARE of the table; the added-call figure is twice that, because each qualifying row pays two extra calls.) At task 04's measured 2.85s/call effective at EXTRACT_MAX_WORKERS=3 (DECISIONS.md:331) that is ~23 minutes of extra wall clock one time. Nightly it is less, and bursty rather than steady: hn_whoishiring is a single monthly thread, so its 247 rows arrive on one night a month and the other 29 nights pay nothing at all.
_rejected_uniform_majority_of_3: Rejected: run three passes on every platform. It pays 3x across 11,824 rows -- 23,648 extra calls, ~19 hours at 2.85s/call -- to fix an instability that measurement locates in 247 of them. Six of the seven platforms are at 91.1% or better, so on those the second and third calls buy a third opinion that agrees with the first nine times in ten. It is also the wrong shape: it makes the fix invisible to whoever next asks 'which sources are we least sure about', where a per-platform table answers that by being read.
_rejected_confidence_field: Rejected: add a confidence field to the prompt and store the model's own self-report instead of voting. It labels the instability without fixing it -- the row written is still one unstable draw -- and it asks the same model that cannot reproduce its own ai_involvement answer to reliably rate how sure it is about it, which is the same quantity being measured and no more trustworthy. vote_unanimity, recorded per row by the vote, is a confidence signal derived from observed behaviour rather than from self-report, and costs nothing extra once the passes are being paid for.
_rejected_status_quo: Rejected: proceed as-is and note the number. Task 06's gate exists to be acted on; ai_involvement below 90% on the messy platform is the row that reads 'stop. Tasks 10 and 13 need rethinking.' Proceeding would have meant tasks 10, 11 and 13 tuning against a signal that is 22.2% coin-flip on the one source that carries the non-tech, non-ATS postings the cohort is aimed at.
_not_a_version_note: Changing anything in this file changes extraction semantics and therefore ought to move schema.FACTS_VERSION -- 'Versions are cache keys' (CLAUDE.md). It deliberately does NOT, yet: task 12 owns the next bump and carries this change with it, so that one re-extraction pays for both. Until then a job_facts row does not record which policy produced it, beyond job_facts.extraction_passes recording how many calls it actually got.
